name: SC16IS752IPW,128
title: SC16IS752 / SC16IS762: dual UART with I2C or SPI host interface, 64-byte FIFOs, IrDA SIR, eight GPIOs
summary: A bridge from an I2C (to 400 kbit/s) or SPI host bus to two independent full-duplex UARTs, each with 64-byte transmit and receive FIFOs and a 16C450-style register set. Serial rates reach 5 Mbit/s with the 16× clock; hardware (RTS/CTS) and Xon/Xoff flow control, automatic RS-485 direction and address detection, and an IrDA SIR coder are built in, and eight GPIOs double as modem lines. It runs from 2.5 V or 3.3 V with 5 V tolerant inputs. The SC16IS762 differs only in a 15 Mbit/s SPI clock (against 4 Mbit/s) and IrDA SIR to 1.152 Mbit/s; both come in TSSOP28 and HVQFN32.
key_figures: 64 bytes TX and 64 bytes RX per channel
I2C 400 kbit/s max (target only) or SPI mode 0 (target only)
2.3 V to 2.7 V or 3.0 V to 3.6 V
2.0 mA max operating, X1 = 4 MHz; 25 μA max in sleep
crystal to 24 MHz; external clock to 48 MHz (2.5 V) or 80 MHz (3.3 V)

After an RX or TX FIFO reset through FCR[1:0], wait at least 2 XTAL1 periods before reading RHR or writing THR.
IIR is not to be read in a burst: no multi-byte I2C read without a STOP or repeated START, and no multi-byte SPI read with CS held LOW.
EFCR[7] selects slow or fast IrDA on the SC16IS762; on the SC16IS752 only the slow mode exists.

tables.title: FIFO Control Register (FCR) bits
rows: TX FIFO trigger level: 00 = 8, 01 = 16, 10 = 32, 11 = 56 spaces; writable only while EFR[4] = 1
TX FIFO reset: 1 empties the transmit FIFO and its level counter, leaving the shift register alone; clears itself
RX FIFO reset: 1 empties the receive FIFO and its level counter, leaving the shift register alone; clears itself
FIFO enable: 0 = both FIFOs off (default), 1 = both on
notes: FCR is write-only.
A FIFO reset takes at least two XTAL1 clock cycles, so it does not happen without a clock on XTAL1.

tables.title: Modem Control Register (MCR) bits
rows: Clock divisor: 0 = divide by 1, 1 = divide by 4
Loopback: 0 = normal, 1 = internal loopback; TX feeds RX and MCR[1:0] feed MSR[4:5]
TCR and TLR enable: 0 = off, 1 = on
RTS: 0 = RTS inactive (HIGH), 1 = RTS active (LOW); drives MSR[4] in loopback; ignored while Auto-RTS controls the pin
DTR, when GPIO5 or GPIO1 is a DTR pin (IOControl bit 1 or 2): 0 = DTR inactive (HIGH), 1 = DTR active (LOW); IOState bits 5 and 1 then have no effect on it

tables.title: Line Status Register (LSR) bits
rows: FIFO data error: 1 = at least one parity, framing or break error somewhere in the RX FIFO; clears when none remain
THR and TSR empty: 1 = holding and shift registers both empty
THR empty: 1 = holding register empty; with the FIFO on, up to 64 characters may be written
Break interrupt: 1 = RX stayed LOW for a whole character time; the character reads 0x00
Framing error: 1 = the character being read from the RX FIFO lacked a valid stop bit
Parity error: 1 = parity error in the character being read from the RX FIFO
Overrun error: 1 = an overrun has happened
Data in receiver: 1 = at least one character in the RX FIFO
notes: LSR[4:2] belong to the character at the head of the RX FIFO, the next one RHR returns; read LSR before RHR to pair errors with characters.

tables.title: Modem Status Register (MSR) bits

RI, inverted from the RI input, when GPIO7 or GPIO3 is an RI pin; IOState bit 7 or 3 does not show the true pin state
DSR, inverted from the DSR input, when GPIO4 or GPIO0 is a DSR pin; IOState bit 4 or 0 does not show the true pin state
CTS, inverted from the CTS input
ΔCD: CD has changed; cleared by reading
ΔRI: RI has gone from LOW to HIGH; cleared by reading
ΔDSR: DSR has changed; cleared by reading
ΔCTS: CTS has changed; cleared by reading
notes: The RI, CD, CTS and DSR pins are active LOW.

tables.title: Transmission Control Register (TCR) bits
rows: RX FIFO level at which transmission resumes
RX FIFO level at which transmission halts
notes: Levels run from 0 to 60 characters in steps of 4.
TCR is written only with EFR[4] = 1 and MCR[2] = 1. TCR[3:0] must exceed TCR[7:4]; the chip does not check it. Program TCR before turning on Auto-RTS or software flow control.
With TCR all zero, the FCR trigger levels are used instead.

tables.title: Trigger Level Register (TLR) bits
rows: RX FIFO trigger level, 4 to 60 characters available
TX FIFO trigger level, 4 to 60 spaces available
notes: TLR is written only with EFR[4] = 1 and MCR[2] = 1. Each field holds N/4 for a trigger level N, in steps of 4.
A field left at 0 hands that FIFO's trigger level back to FCR; a non-zero field overrides FCR. When TLR sets the RX level, FCR[7:6] stays at 00.

tables.title: Transmitter FIFO Level register (TXLVL) bits

notes: Read-only.

tables.title: Receiver FIFO Level register (RXLVL) bits

notes: Read-only.

tables.title: IOState register bits

tables.title: IOIntEna register bits

tables.title: IOControl register bits
rows: software reset: writing 1 resets the device; the bit then reads 0
GPIO[3:0] or RIB, CDB, DTRB, DSRB
0 = GPIO3 to GPIO0 are I/O pins, 1 = they act as RIB, CDB, DTRB, DSRB
GPIO[7:4] or RIA, CDA, DTRA, DSRA
0 = GPIO7 to GPIO4 are I/O pins, 1 = they act as RIA, CDA, DTRA, DSRA

input latching. 0: no latch; any input change interrupts, reading the input register clears it, and the interrupt also clears if the pin returns to its old level first. 1: latched; the changed level is held in IOState and the interrupt stays until IOState is read, even if the pin returns
notes: As I/O pins, the GPIOs are run by IODir, IOState, IOIntEna and IOControl; CD, RI and DSR then do not appear in MSR or raise modem interrupts, and MCR[0] does not drive DTR.
As modem pins, CD, RI and DSR are read in MSR[7:5] and MSR[3:1], DTR follows MCR[0], IER[3] enables their interrupt, and IODir, IOState and IOIntEna do not affect them.

circuits.title: Crystal oscillator
circuits.description: A 1.8432 MHz crystal across XTAL1 and XTAL2 makes the clock with the on-chip oscillator. Each crystal end has its own load capacitor to ground: 22 pF on XTAL1 and 33 pF on XTAL2. The 1.8432 MHz baud table gives the divisors for this crystal.

equations.name: Baud rate divisor

where.divisor: 16-bit value written to DLH (high byte) and DLL (low byte), 1 to 2^16 - 1
where.fXTAL1: crystal or external clock frequency on XTAL1
where.prescaler: 1 with MCR[7] = 0 (the reset state), 4 with MCR[7] = 1

equations.note: The baud generator output is 16 times the baud rate. DLL = DLH = 0 stops the baud clock, which disables the UART.

where.N: wanted FIFO trigger level, 4 to 60 in steps of 4

operation.text: The SC16IS762 takes an SPI clock up to 15 Mbit/s and runs IrDA SIR up to 1.152 Mbit/s; the SC16IS752 stops at 4 Mbit/s SPI and 115.2 kbit/s IrDA. Everything else is shared. IrDA SIR at 1.152 Mbit/s does not interoperate with IrDA MIR at that rate.

Two full-duplex UART channels, each 16C450-compatible with 64-byte FIFOs, with serial rates as high as 5 Mbit/s using the 16× clock. Automatic RTS/CTS flow control; Xon/Xoff flow control with single or double programmable characters; automatic RS-485 address detection and RTS direction control with optional inversion; software reset; independent transmitter and receiver enables; readable FIFO levels; special-character detection; 5 to 8 data bits, even/odd/no parity, 1, 1½ or 2 stop bits; sending and detecting breaks; an internal loop-back mode. Sleep current is under 30 μA at 3.3 V. Inputs are 5 V tolerant. Industrial range -40 °C to +95 °C.
The I2C/SPI pin picks the host bus: HIGH for I2C, LOW for SPI. In SPI mode the SDA pin is tied to VSS; in I2C mode SO is left open and CS/A0 and SI/A1 become address inputs.

The chip is an I2C target only, Fast mode (400 kbit/s max), with spike filters on SCL and SDA. Each of A1 and A0 can be strapped to VDD, VSS, SCL or SDA, giving 16 addresses from 0x90 to 0xAE (8-bit form). The serial interface resets itself if SDA is held LOW for 25 ms or longer, which sets the lowest usable SCL rate.

After the address byte comes a subaddress byte: bits 6:3 pick the register, bits 2:1 the channel (00 for A, 01 for B), bits 7 and 0 unused. A write continues with data bytes written in turn to that register. A read writes the subaddress, then sends a repeated START with the address in read mode; data bytes follow, each acknowledged by the host, and the last is answered with a not-acknowledge before the STOP.

SPI mode 0, target only. CS LOW frames a transfer. The first byte is the register address byte: bit 7 is R/W (1 = read), bits 6:3 the register, bits 2:1 the channel, bit 0 unused. A single data byte follows for a register access. Addressing register 0x00 (RHR/THR) and keeping CS LOW moves successive bytes into the TX FIFO or out of the RX FIFO. SO is high-impedance while CS is HIGH.

Each channel has a 64-character TX FIFO and a 64-character RX FIFO; the RX FIFO also keeps three error bits per character. Both FIFOs are off after reset, so the effective trigger level is one character. FCR offers fixed trigger levels; TLR sets them in steps of 4 from 4 to 60 and, when non-zero, takes precedence. TXLVL and RXLVL report the free TX spaces and the stored RX characters.

With EFR[6] set, RTS stays asserted while the RX FIFO is below the TCR[3:0] halt level and is released once that level is reached. The far transmitter may still send one more character after release. RTS is asserted again when the FIFO drains to the TCR[7:4] resume level. With TCR at zero the FCR levels are used.

With EFR[7] set, the transmitter checks CTS before each character. CTS released while a character is going out still lets that character finish; if the release comes ahead of the midpoint of its final stop bit, no further character starts. CTS changes raise no host interrupt while Auto-CTS runs. Linking RTS to CTS between two such UARTs with both features on prevents receive overruns.

EFR[3:0] choose which Xon/Xoff characters are sent and compared. When the right Xoff arrives, transmission stops after the current character, IIR[4] is set if IER[5] allows and IRQ goes LOW; the matching Xon clears it and restarts. The chip sends Xoff when the RX FIFO passes the TCR[3:0] or FCR halt level and Xon at the TCR[7:4] resume level or below the lower FCR level. Flow characters follow the programmed word length, so only their low 5, 6 or 7 bits go out in shorter formats. Xon Any (MCR[5]) lets any received character restart transmission. Special character detect (EFR[5]) compares incoming bytes with Xoff2, sets the Xoff interrupt without halting, stores the byte in the FIFO, and is cleared by an IIR read. Hardware and software flow control are not meant to run at the same time.

The RESET pin (active LOW), power-on reset and the IOControl software reset bit all reset the registers the same way (reset state table). After reset TX and RTS are HIGH, the GPIOs are inputs, and IRQ sits HIGH on its pull-up. The reset pulse is 3 μs minimum; the first SCL edge may follow 3 μs (or 2 XTAL1 cycles, whichever is less) after reset ends.

Seven prioritised interrupt types are enabled through IER and IOIntEna and signalled on the open-drain IRQ pin; IIR[5:0] names the highest one pending. Framing, parity and break errors reach the host through LSR[7], which stays set while any errored character remains in the RX FIFO. An Xoff interrupt caused by an Xoff character clears when Xon arrives; one caused by a special character clears on an IIR read. With any of IER[3:0] set the part runs interrupt-driven; with IER[3:0] = 0000 the host polls LSR.

Sleep is allowed when EFR[4] and IER[4] are both set, and is entered once RX is idle, the TX FIFO and shift register are empty, the RX FIFO is empty and no interrupt except THR is pending. The UART clock then stops. Any activity on RX, any modem input change, or a write to the TX FIFO wakes it. DLL and DLH are not to be written in sleep; clear IER[4] first.

If characters sit in the RX FIFO below the trigger level, a time-out interrupt fires 4 character times after the last one arrived; the counter restarts at each received stop bit centre and at each FIFO read. A break is detected when RX stays LOW longer than one full character frame including start, parity and stop bits. Setting LCR[6] sends a break by holding TX LOW.

The XTAL1 clock, divided by 1 or by 4 (MCR[7]), feeds a 16-bit divider whose output is 16 times the baud rate; the same rate serves transmit and receive. The divide-by-1 prescaler is the reset default. The baud tables give divisors and error for 1.8432 MHz and 3.072 MHz crystals.
A crystal between XTAL1 and XTAL2 runs with the internal oscillator up to 24 MHz. An external clock into XTAL1 may run up to 48 MHz at 2.5 V or 80 MHz at 3.3 V, with XTAL2 left open.

Writing LCR[7] = 1 opens the divisor latches DLL and DLH in place of the general registers at the same addresses. Writing LCR = 0xBF opens EFR and the four Xon/Xoff words. TCR and TLR appear at 0x06 and 0x07 when EFR[4] = 1 and MCR[2] = 1. EFR[4] also unlocks IER[7:4], FCR[5:4] and MCR[7:5].

GPIO0 to GPIO7 are set as inputs or outputs in IODir and read or written through IOState; IOIntEna enables an interrupt on input changes, and IOControl bit 0 chooses whether input changes are latched. IOControl bit 2 turns GPIO3:0 into the channel B modem lines RI, CD, DTR, DSR, and bit 1 turns GPIO7:4 into the channel A lines. As modem lines their inputs appear (inverted) in MSR and their interrupt comes from IER[3]; DTR follows MCR[0].

With EFCR[4] set the transmitter owns RTS, overriding MCR[1] and Auto-RTS: RTS goes LOW when the host loads the TX FIFO and HIGH after the last bit leaves. EFCR[5] inverts that sense. Hardware flow control has to be off in this mode.

EFCR[0] selects 9-bit mode, in which the parity bit marks address characters (1) apart from data (0). Without special character detect, the receiver is set to forced parity 0 (LCR[5:3] = 111); each address byte then shows as a parity error, raises a line status interrupt (IER[2] set) and enters the RX FIFO, and the host enables or disables the receiver depending on whether the address is its own.

With EFR[5] set and the station address loaded in XOFF2, the receiver drops data and non-matching addresses on its own. A matching address enables the receiver, goes into the RX FIFO with its parity bit in the parity-error position, and raises a line status interrupt (IER[2] set). A later address that does not match disables the receiver again and is discarded.
MCR[6] switches a channel to IrDA SIR coding. EFCR[7] = 0 gives 3/16-bit pulses up to 115.2 kbit/s; EFCR[7] = 1, on the SC16IS762 only, gives 1/4-bit pulses up to 1.152 Mbit/s.
MCR[4] = 1 links TX to RX inside the chip and feeds MCR[1:0] back into the modem status bits; the TX pin is cut off from the transmitter and the RX pin is ignored.
Inputs take up to 5.5 V steady state while VDD is present. Unpowered, the steady-state limit is 4.6 V among the limiting values and 3.8 V among the static characteristics.
The die ground connects to the VSS pins and to the exposed pad. All VSS pins go to ground; the pad is soldered to a matching board land with thermal vias for heat and electrical performance.
All pins have ESD protection for normal handling; precautions per JESD625-A or equivalent apply.

Revision D silicon cannot wake from sleep through the RX pin, and cannot clear an overflowed RX FIFO with a FIFO reset while data keeps arriving. An IIR read whose internal read edge falls close to the XTAL1 edge that raises an interrupt may return a wrong value; this is most likely with a slow XTAL1 clock and a fast host. An RX FIFO read that coincides with a time-out may give IIR = 0xCC while LSR[0] = 0.
